questions.question: In which of the following cities of British India was the Communist Party of India founded, in 1925?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Communist Party of India (CPI) was founded in **Kanpur** in December 1925.
 
• Key founding members included **M.N. Roy, Abani Mukherji, and Shripad Amrit Dange**.
 
• The founding meeting took place at Kanpur where various labor and peasant movements were discussed.
 
• The CPI was established with the aim of promoting **Marxist-Leninist ideology** and working towards the rights of the proletariat in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Communist Party of India (CPI)**

 
 
• The CPI is one of the oldest political parties in India, aimed at establishing a socialist state.
 
• The party played a significant role in India's struggle for independence and post-independence politics.
 
• The CPI split in 1964, leading to the formation of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) or CPI(M).
 
• The CPI is part of the Left Front in Indian politics and has been influential in several states, particularly in West Bengal, Kerala, and Tripura.
 
 
 
• **Marxist-Leninist Ideology**
 
 
• This ideology is based on the theories of Karl Marx and Vladimir Lenin.
 
• It advocates for the overthrow of the capitalist system and establishment of a dictatorship of the proletariat.
 
• The ultimate goal is to achieve a classless, stateless society through the means of revolutionary socialism.
 
 
 
• **Labor and Peasant Movements**
 
 
• The labor and peasant movements were crucial in mobilizing the working class and rural population against British rule.
 
• These movements aimed to address issues such as land reforms, workers' rights, and better wages.
 
• They were instrumental in the formation of various trade unions and peasant associations.
 
 
 
• **Role in Indian Independence**
 
 
• The CPI actively participated in the anti-colonial struggle and collaborated with other nationalist forces.
 
• Despite ideological differences with the Indian National Congress, the CPI supported mass movements like the Quit India Movement.
 
• Post-independence, the CPI continued to work towards socio-economic reforms and workers' rights.

questions.question: During the census 2011, which of the following states recorded the lowest growth rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the 2011 Census, Nagaland recorded the lowest population growth rate among Indian states.
 
• The state experienced a negative growth rate of -0.47% between 2001 and 2011.
 
• Nagaland's population decreased from 1,990,036 in 2001 to 1,978,502 in 2011.
 
• This decline is attributed to migration to other states and errors in the previous census enumeration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census in India**

 
 
• The Census of India is a decennial exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The first complete census was conducted in 1881, and since then, it has been conducted every ten years.
 
• The census provides comprehensive data on the demographic, social, and economic characteristics of the population.
 
 
 
• **Population Growth Rate**
 
 
• The population growth rate is the rate at which the number of individuals in a population increases in a given time period as a fraction of the initial population.
 
• It is an important indicator of demographic trends and is influenced by factors such as birth rate, death rate, and migration.
 
 
 
• **Migration**
 
 
• Migration refers to the movement of people from one place to another, which can be within a country (internal migration) or between countries (international migration).
 
• Migration can significantly impact the population size and composition of both the origin and destination areas.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Trends**
 
 
• Demographic trends refer to the changes in the population over time, including changes in size, composition, and distribution.
 
• Understanding these trends is crucial for policy-making, planning, and resource allocation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with regard to the effect of globalisation on India and other developing countries?

options.text: Flow of information became highly restricted.
It led to increased inequality between countries.
Flow of international capital got restricted.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It led to increased inequality between countries.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Globalization has often resulted in widening the gap between developed and developing countries due to differences in economic, technological, and resource capacities.
 
• Developing countries like India have faced challenges in competing with developed nations, leading to increased economic disparities.
 
• The benefits of globalization have not been equally distributed, with wealthier nations often reaping more significant advantages.
 
• Globalization has sometimes exacerbated income inequality within countries, as certain sectors and regions benefit more than others.
 
• While globalization has led to significant economic growth, it has also highlighted and sometimes deepened existing inequalities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalization:**

 
 
• The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
 
• It involves the increased interconnectedness and interdependence of economies, societies, and cultures through cross-border trade, investment, and information technology.
 
 
 
• **Economic Disparities:**
 
 
• Differences in income, wealth, and economic opportunities between different groups within a society or between different countries.
 
• Can be measured by indicators such as the Gini coefficient, which assesses income inequality within a population.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancement:**
 
 
• Refers to the development and application of new tools, machines, and techniques that help improve efficiency and productivity.
 
• While technological progress can drive economic growth, it can also lead to job displacement and increased inequality if not managed inclusively.
 
 
 
• **Trade Liberalization:**
 
 
• The removal or reduction of trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas to facilitate easier and more efficient cross-border trade.
 
• Can lead to increased market access for businesses but may also result in domestic industries facing stiff competition from foreign firms.
 
 
 
• **Income Inequality:**
 
 
• The unequal distribution of income within a population, where some individuals or groups earn significantly more than others.
 
• High levels of income inequality can have social and economic repercussions, including reduced social mobility and increased social tensions.

questions.question: Guru Amubi Singh won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for which form of dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Guru Amubi Singh is a renowned exponent of Manipuri dance.
 
• Manipuri dance, also known as Jagoi, is one of the major Indian classical dance forms.
 
• The dance form originated in the northeastern state of Manipur in India.
 
• Manipuri dance is known for its graceful and delicate movements, often depicting themes related to the love story of Radha and Krishna.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is a prestigious award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama, to recognize outstanding achievement in the performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History and Origin of Manipuri Dance:**

 
 
• Manipuri dance has its roots in the ancient rituals and traditional festivals of Manipur.
 
• It is closely associated with the rituals and religious festivities of the Vaishnavism sect.
 
• The dance form gained prominence during the reign of Maharaja Bhagya Chandra in the 18th century.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Manipuri Dance:**
 
 
• Manipuri dance is characterized by smooth, graceful, and fluid movements.
 
• The dance form emphasizes hand gestures, facial expressions, and body movements.
 
• It often involves intricate footwork and rhythmic patterns.
 
 
 
• **Costumes and Music:**
 
 
• The costumes in Manipuri dance are elaborate and colorful, often made of traditional silk and adorned with intricate designs.
 
• The music accompanying the dance is typically based on classical Indian ragas and talas.
 
• Traditional instruments such as the Pung (a type of drum) and Kartal (cymbals) are commonly used in Manipuri dance performances.
 
 
 
• **Notable Exponents:**
 
 
• Besides Guru Amubi Singh, other notable exponents of Manipuri dance include Guru Bipin Singh, Nirmala Mehta, and Darshana Jhaveri.

questions.question: The Teliaya Dam is located in which state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Teliaya Dam is situated in the Hazaribagh district of Jharkhand.
 
• It was constructed on the Barakar River, a tributary of the Damodar River.
 
• The dam is part of the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) project, which was one of the first multipurpose river valley projects in India.
 
• Teliaya Dam was inaugurated in 1953 and is primarily used for flood control, irrigation, and power generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC)**

 
 
• DVC is a government organization that operates in the Damodar River region of India.
 
• It was established in 1948 for integrated development of the Damodar River basin.
 
• DVC's main objectives include flood control, irrigation, generation, and transmission of electricity.
 
• The corporation manages several dams, reservoirs, and thermal power plants in the region.
 
 
 
• **Barakar River**
 
 
• The Barakar River is the main tributary of the Damodar River.
 
• It flows through the states of Jharkhand and West Bengal.
 
• The river is crucial for irrigation and water supply in the region.
 
 
 
• **Multipurpose River Valley Projects**
 
 
• These projects aim to achieve multiple objectives like flood control, irrigation, power generation, and water supply.
 
• The Damodar Valley Project is one of India's first major multipurpose river valley projects.
 
• Such projects help in the sustainable management of water resources.

questions.question: Who among the following dancers and choreographers is credited to bring fusion art into a dance where European style is mixed with Indian Classical Dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uday Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uday Shankar is renowned for pioneering the fusion of European ballet and Indian classical dance, creating a unique dance style.
 
• He is often credited with bringing Indian dance to the international stage through his innovative choreography and performances.
 
• Uday Shankar trained under Anna Pavlova, a famous Russian ballerina, which significantly influenced his fusion style.
 
• His dance company, established in the 1930s, played a crucial role in popularizing Indian dance forms and fusion art globally.
 
• Uday Shankar's work has inspired many contemporary dancers and choreographers, bridging the gap between Eastern and Western dance traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Classical Dance Forms**

 
 
• India is home to several classical dance forms, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, and Mohiniyattam.
 
• Each dance form has its own unique style, costumes, and musical accompaniment.
 
• Classical dances are deeply rooted in Indian culture and are often based on ancient texts and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Fusion Dance**
 
 
• Fusion dance combines elements from different dance styles to create a new, hybrid form.
 
• It allows for creative expression and innovation, often blending classical, contemporary, and folk traditions.
 
• Fusion dance can be seen in various performances, from stage shows to music videos.
 
 
 
• **Anna Pavlova**
 
 
• Anna Pavlova was a renowned Russian prima ballerina of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• She is best known for her role in "The Dying Swan," which became synonymous with her name.
 
• Pavlova's influence extended beyond ballet, inspiring dancers worldwide, including Uday Shankar.
 
 
 
• **Contemporary Dance**
 
 
• Contemporary dance is a genre that developed during the mid-20th century and continues to evolve.
 
• It incorporates elements from various dance styles, including modern, jazz, lyrical, and classical ballet.
 
• Contemporary dance emphasizes versatility, improvisation, and expression.

questions.question: Which scheme was rolled out to effectively integrate India’s manufacturing capabilities with the demands of global supply chains and to promote domestic value addition and exports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Production Linked Incentive Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme was launched by the Government of India to boost manufacturing in the country.
 
• It aims to promote domestic manufacturing and reduce import dependence by providing incentives based on incremental sales from products manufactured in India.
 
• The scheme covers key sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, and textiles, among others.
 
• The PLI Scheme is designed to attract large-scale investments, enhance the competitiveness of Indian products, and integrate India into the global supply chain.
 
• As of 2023, the government has expanded the scheme to include more sectors and increase the financial outlay to further stimulate manufacturing growth in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Make in India Initiative**

 
 
• Launched in 2014, it aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub by encouraging both multinational and domestic companies to manufacture their products in India.
 
• The initiative focuses on key sectors such as automobiles, chemicals, IT, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and more.
 
• It aims to increase the manufacturing sector's contribution to the GDP to 25% by 2025.
 
• Make in India promotes ease of doing business, innovation, skill development, and intellectual property rights.
 
 
 
• **Startup India**
 
 
• Launched in 2016, this initiative aims to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and startups in India.
 
• It focuses on simplifying regulatory frameworks, providing funding support, and fostering an entrepreneurial culture.
 
• Startup India offers various benefits including tax exemptions, patent filing support, and credit guarantee schemes.
 
 
 
• **Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)**
 
 
• Introduced in 2015, MEIS aims to promote the export of notified goods manufactured in India.
 
• Under the scheme, exporters are rewarded with duty credit scrips which can be used to pay various duties and taxes.
 
• MEIS has been replaced by the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Export Products (RoDTEP) scheme from January 1, 2021.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat**
 
 
• Launched in 2020, it aims to make India self-reliant by promoting local products and reducing dependence on imports.
 
• It encompasses various measures including reforms in agriculture, MSMEs, and defense manufacturing.
 
• The initiative also focuses on boosting infrastructure, improving governance, and ensuring ease of doing business.

• The autobiography highlights the Tibetan struggle for freedom and the Dalai Lama's efforts to preserve Tibetan culture and identity.
 
• The book is widely regarded as an important work for understanding the life and philosophy of the Dalai Lama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **14th Dalai Lama**

 
 
• Born on July 6, 1935, as Lhamo Thondup in Taktser, Amdo, Tibet.
 
• Recognized as the reincarnation of the 13th Dalai Lama at the age of two.
 
• Enthroned as the spiritual leader of Tibet in 1940.
 
• Fled to India in 1959 following the Tibetan uprising against Chinese rule.
 
• Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his non-violent struggle for the liberation of Tibet.
 
 
 
• **Tibetan Buddhism**
 
 
• A form of Mahayana Buddhism that evolved in Tibet and the Himalayan region.
 
• Combines the essential teachings of Mahayana Buddhism with Tantric and Shamanic elements.
 
• The Dalai Lama is considered the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism.
 
• Focuses on the path to enlightenment through meditation, moral conduct, and wisdom.
 
 
 
• **Tibetan Government in Exile**
 
 
• Also known as the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA).
 
• Established in 1959 after the Dalai Lama and thousands of Tibetans fled to India.
 
• Based in Dharamshala, India.
 
• Works to preserve Tibetan culture, promote human rights, and seek a peaceful resolution to the Tibet issue.
 
 
 
• **Non-violence and Compassion**
 
 
• Core principles advocated by the Dalai Lama.
 
• Emphasizes the importance of compassion, kindness, and forgiveness.

questions.question: From which country did India import wheat seeds during the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mexico**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the Green Revolution, India imported high-yielding variety (HYV) wheat seeds from Mexico.
 
• The imported seeds were developed by Dr. Norman Borlaug, who is often called the "Father of the Green Revolution."
 
• These Mexican seeds played a crucial role in significantly increasing wheat production in India.
 
• The introduction of these seeds led to higher agricultural productivity and helped India achieve self-sufficiency in food grains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s.
 
• It was aimed at increasing agricultural production globally, particularly in developing countries.
 
• Major components included the development of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of staple crops, expansion of irrigation infrastructure, and the use of fertilizers and pesticides.
 
 
 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYVs)**
 
 
• HYVs are crops that have been specifically bred to produce more grain per acre compared to traditional varieties.
 
• They typically require more inputs such as water, fertilizers, and pesticides to achieve their high yields.
 
 
 
• **Impact on India**
 
 
• The Green Revolution led to a substantial increase in food grain production, particularly in the states of Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It transformed India from a food-deficient country to one of the world's leading agricultural nations.
 
 
 
• **Norman Borlaug**
 
 
• Norman Borlaug was an American agronomist known for his work in developing high-yielding crop varieties.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contributions to increasing global food supplies.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of budget of the Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Circle budget**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Surplus budget**: A budget in which the expected government revenues exceed the planned government expenditures.
 
• **Deficit budget**: A budget where the government’s expenditures surpass its revenues, resulting in a deficit.
 
• **Balanced budget**: A budget in which the revenues are equal to the expenditures, resulting in neither a surplus nor a deficit.
 
• **Circle budget**: This term does not refer to any recognized type of government budget.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal policy**:

 
 
• Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and tax policies to influence economic conditions, especially macroeconomic conditions such as growth, employment, and inflation.
 
• There are two main instruments of fiscal policy: government expenditure and taxation.
 
 
 
• **Types of government budgets**:
 
 
• **Surplus Budget**: When revenue exceeds expenditure.
 
• **Deficit Budget**: When expenditure exceeds revenue.
 
• **Balanced Budget**: When revenue equals expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Budget Deficit**:
 
 
• A budget deficit occurs when expenses exceed revenue, and it indicates the financial health of a country.
 
• Governments usually borrow to cover the deficit, leading to national debt.
 
 
 
• **National Debt**:
 
 
• National debt is the total amount of money that a country's government has borrowed, by various means.
 
• It is a measure of a government's financial obligations.

questions.question: Stainless steel cookware contains _______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**chromium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Stainless steel is an alloy primarily made of iron, carbon, and chromium.
 
• Chromium content in stainless steel typically ranges from 10.5% to 30% by weight.
 
• Chromium is added to stainless steel to provide corrosion resistance by forming a passive layer of chromium oxide on the surface.
 
• This passive layer prevents rust and other forms of corrosion, significantly enhancing the durability and longevity of the cookware.
 
• Stainless steel's non-reactive nature makes it ideal for cooking, as it does not interact with acidic or alkaline foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Stainless Steel**

 
 
• **Austenitic Stainless Steel:** Contains high levels of chromium and nickel, known for its excellent corrosion resistance and formability.
 
• **Ferritic Stainless Steel:** Contains chromium but little to no nickel, offering good corrosion resistance and magnetic properties.
 
• **Martensitic Stainless Steel:** Contains higher carbon content, known for its hardness and strength, but less corrosion resistance compared to austenitic and ferritic types.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chromium in Stainless Steel**
 
 
• Chromium enhances corrosion resistance by forming a stable, adherent oxide layer on the surface.
 
• It improves the hardness and tensile strength of the alloy.
 
• Chromium also increases the wear and oxidation resistance of stainless steel.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Stainless Steel**
 
 
• Used extensively in kitchen appliances, cookware, cutlery, and medical instruments due to its non-reactive and durable nature.
 
• Commonly employed in construction, automotive, and aerospace industries for its structural integrity and resistance to environmental stressors.
 
• Utilized in the manufacturing of chemical and food processing equipment due to its ability to withstand harsh chemical environments.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the District Planning Committee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 243-ZD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 243-ZD of the Indian Constitution mandates the establishment of a District Planning Committee (DPC) in every state at the district level.
 
• The primary function of the DPC is to consolidate the plans prepared by the Panchayats and Municipalities in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.
 
• The DPC is required to consider matters of common interest between the Panchayats and the Municipalities, including spatial planning, sharing of water and other physical and natural resources, integrated development of infrastructure, and environmental conservation.
 
• The composition of the DPC and the manner of electing members to such committees are to be prescribed by the legislature of the state.
 
• Not less than four-fifths of the members of the DPC are to be elected by the elected members of the Panchayat at the district level and the Municipalities in the district from amongst themselves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**

 
 
• PRIs are the rural local self-government institutions in India.
 
• They operate at three levels: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zilla Parishad (district level).
 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided constitutional status to the PRIs.
 
• PRIs aim to promote decentralized governance, ensuring greater participation of people in decision-making processes.
 
 
 
• **Municipalities**
 
 
• Municipalities are urban local self-government institutions.
 
• They are responsible for providing basic amenities and civic services to urban areas.
 
• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided constitutional status to municipalities.
 
• There are different types of municipalities: Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, and Nagar Panchayats, depending on the size and population of the urban area.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments Related to Local Governance**
 
 
• The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts were passed in 1992 to strengthen and empower local self-governments in rural and urban areas, respectively.
 
• These amendments introduced Articles 243 to 243-O (for PRIs) and Articles 243-P to 243-ZG (for Municipalities) in the Indian Constitution.
 
• They also mandated the creation of State Election Commissions to conduct elections to local bodies.
 
• The amendments aimed to ensure the participation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in local governance through reservation of seats.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Development Planning**
 
 
• Integrated development planning involves the coordinated efforts of various government agencies and local bodies to achieve balanced and sustainable development.
 
• It takes into account economic, social, environmental, and physical aspects of development.
 
• District Planning Committees play a crucial role in integrated development planning by consolidating plans from different local bodies within the district.
 
• This approach aims to address disparities and promote equitable development across different regions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about plastids is INCORRECT?

options.text: Leucoplasts are primarily organelles in which materials such as starch, oils and protein granules are stored.
Leucoplasts are white or colourless plastids.
Plastids do not have their own DNA and ribosomes.
Chromoplasts are responsible for photosynthesis in plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastids do not have their own DNA and ribosomes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plastids, including chloroplasts, leucoplasts, and chromoplasts, do contain their own DNA and ribosomes.
 
• Plastid DNA is circular and similar to bacterial DNA, reflecting their evolutionary origin.
 
• Due to their own DNA and ribosomes, plastids can produce some of their own proteins independently of the cell's nuclear DNA.
 
• The presence of their own genetic material is a key feature distinguishing plastids from other organelles like the endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leucoplasts**

 
 
• They are colorless plastids found in non-photosynthetic tissues of plants.
 
• Primarily involved in the storage of starch, oils, and proteins.
 
• Leucoplasts can differentiate into other forms of plastids based on the plant’s needs.
 
 
 
• **Chromoplasts**
 
 
• Chromoplasts contain pigments like carotenoids, which give yellow, red, and orange colors to various plant parts.
 
• They are involved in the synthesis and storage of pigments, aiding in the process of pollination by attracting pollinators.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplasts**
 
 
• Chloroplasts are green plastids responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells.
 
• They contain chlorophyll, which captures light energy for the synthesis of glucose.
 
• Chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes, similar to other plastids.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**
 
 
• This theory explains the origin of plastids and mitochondria as formerly free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by early eukaryotic cells.
 
• Both organelles have their own circular DNA and ribosomes similar to bacteria, supporting this theory.

questions.question: The Constitution (42ⁿd Amendment) Act, 1976, Chapter IV-A introduced a code of ten _____________ for citizens.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Duties**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1976**, introduced the concept of Fundamental Duties.
 
• These duties are outlined in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution under Article **51A**.
 
• Originally, the amendment included **ten Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens.
 
• These duties were added based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• One more duty was added later, making the total **eleven Fundamental Duties** currently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union (USSR).
 
• They serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they should also perform their duties towards the country.
 
• They are not enforceable by law, but they are considered essential for promoting a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• Some examples include respecting the national symbols, cherishing the heritage, and protecting the environment.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**
 
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution and are aimed at guiding the state in policy-making and legislation.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts.
 
• They were inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Examples include provisions for adequate livelihood, equal pay for equal work, and promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution and are considered essential for the overall development of individuals.
 
• They are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• Examples include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• These rights are essential for the protection of individual liberty and democratic principles in the country.

questions.question: What does LPG cooking gas contain?

• These hydrocarbons are obtained during the refining of crude oil or extracted from natural gas streams.
 
• Propane and butane are stored in liquid form under moderate pressure, making them easily transportable and storable.
 
• When released from the storage container, they return to gaseous form for use in cooking, heating, and other applications.

• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• LPG burns more cleanly than other fossil fuels, producing fewer pollutants like carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, and particulates.
 
• It is considered a greener alternative to traditional biomass fuels used in many households.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations:**
 
 
• LPG is highly flammable, and proper safety measures must be adhered to during storage and use.
 
 
• **Applications:**

questions.question: Under which Constitutional Amendment Act were the Fundamental Duties first added to the Indian Constitution?

__
 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in **1976** during the Emergency period in India.
 
• This Amendment added a new part, Part IVA, to the Indian Constitution, which enshrines the **Fundamental Duties** of citizens.
 
• It introduced **10 Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens, inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile Soviet Union.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are listed in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The objective was to emphasize the responsibility of citizens in upholding the unity and integrity of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the 42nd Amendment**

 
 
• The 42nd Amendment is often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its extensive changes to the Constitution.
 
• It was enacted during the tenure of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• This amendment brought about significant changes in the Preamble, Seventh Schedule, and other parts of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts.
 
• They serve as moral obligations for citizens to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among them.
 
• Examples include respecting the national symbols, protecting the environment, and promoting harmony.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the courts, unlike Fundamental Duties.
 
• Both are aimed at ensuring the dignity of individuals and the unity of the nation.
 
• While Fundamental Rights focus on the individual's liberties, Fundamental Duties emphasize collective responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Amendments**
 
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 added an 11th Fundamental Duty, which mandates parents to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6-14 years.
 
• This amendment was part of efforts to implement the Right to Education Act, 2009.

questions.question: Which directive principle provides for a uniform civil code for citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 44 of the Indian Constitution pertains to the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It mandates the State to endeavor to secure a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) for all citizens across the territory of India.
 
• The objective of Article 44 is to provide uniformity in laws relating to marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, and maintenance.
 
• The UCC aims to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set of rules governing every citizen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• The Directive Principles are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution of India from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• Unlike the Fundamental Rights, these principles are non-justiciable, which means they are not enforceable by any court.
 
• They are aimed at ensuring social and economic democracy in the country.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)**
 
 
• The UCC proposes a single law for the country, applicable to all religious communities in their personal matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption.
 
• It seeks to ensure gender equality and national integration.
 
• The implementation of UCC remains a contentious issue with debates over its impact on religious freedom and cultural diversity.
 
 
 
• **Personal Laws in India**
 
 
• Currently, personal laws in India are governed by the religious texts and customs of various communities.
 
• For instance, Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, and Jains are governed by Hindu personal laws, while Muslims and Christians have their own personal laws.
 
• These laws cover aspects such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and maintenance.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions**
 
 
• The Constitution of India provides for both the protection of religious freedom and the pursuit of a UCC.
 
• Article 25 guarantees freedom of religion, while Article 44 advocates for a UCC.
 
• Balancing these provisions remains a complex issue in the legal and social framework of India.

questions.question: According to the Köppen classification, which group of climate is generally found at higher latitudes or higher altitudes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**E group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Köppen classification system categorizes climate types based on temperature and precipitation patterns.
 
• The E group in the Köppen classification represents polar climates.
 
• Polar climates (E group) are generally found at higher latitudes, such as the Arctic and Antarctic regions.
 
• These climates are characterized by extremely cold temperatures throughout the year, with the warmest month having an average temperature below 10°C (50°F).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Köppen Climate Classification**

 
 
• Developed by Wladimir Köppen, it is one of the most widely used climate classification systems.
 
• It categorizes the world's climates into five main groups: A (tropical), B (dry), C (temperate), D (continental), and E (polar).
 
• Each main group is further divided into subgroups based on specific temperature and precipitation criteria.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Polar Climates (E group)**
 
 
• Extremely cold temperatures with long, harsh winters and short, cool summers.
 
• Low precipitation, mostly in the form of snow.
 
• Permafrost and ice caps are common features in these regions.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Polar Climate Zones**
 
 
• The Arctic region, including parts of Canada, Russia, Greenland, and the Arctic Ocean.
 
• The Antarctic region, primarily the continent of Antarctica.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Ecosystems**
 
 
• Poor soil quality and limited vegetation due to the harsh climate.
 
• Adaptations in wildlife, such as thick fur and fat layers in animals like polar bears and seals.
 
• Vulnerable to climate change, with rising temperatures leading to melting ice caps and changes in habitat.

questions.question: In which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India, is it mentioned that “it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture”?

__
 
• Article 51A (f) of the Constitution of India specifies the fundamental duty of every citizen to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• Fundamental duties are listed in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution, which was incorporated by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• These duties are moral obligations intended to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• Article 51A (f) aims to ensure that citizens acknowledge and contribute to the preservation of India's diverse cultural heritage.
 
• Preserving cultural heritage helps in maintaining national identity and promoting unity in diversity.

• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties are inspired by the Constitution of former USSR and are outlined in Part IVA under Article 51A.
 
• There are a total of 11 Fundamental Duties listed for Indian citizens.
 
• They emphasize the importance of respecting national symbols, cherishing the heritage, and upholding the unity and integrity of the nation.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution," this amendment brought about significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added the words "Socialist" and "Secular" to the Preamble.
 
• It also introduced Fundamental Duties and changed the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• The amendment aimed to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the power of the central government.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Heritage**
 
 
• Cultural heritage includes tangible assets such as monuments, artifacts, and intangible assets such as traditions, languages, and practices.
 
• Preservation of cultural heritage promotes tourism, education, and national pride.
 
• UNESCO plays a crucial role in the protection and preservation of world cultural heritage through the World Heritage Sites program.
 
• India has numerous UNESCO World Heritage Sites, showcasing its rich and diverse cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Unity in Diversity**
 
 
• India is known for its vast diversity in terms of languages, religions, cultures, and traditions.
 
• The concept of "Unity in Diversity" signifies that despite these differences, people can coexist harmoniously.
 
• This principle is a cornerstone of Indian society and is reflected in its Constitution.
 
• Promoting unity in diversity strengthens national integrity and social cohesion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salman Rushdie**

 
 
• He is an Indian-born British-American novelist and essayist known for his magical realism and historical fiction.
 
• His most famous work, **Midnight's Children**, won the Booker Prize in 1981.
 
• Rushdie's fourth novel, **The Satanic Verses**, led to considerable controversy and a fatwa calling for his assassination issued by Iran's Ayatollah Khomeini.
 
• His narrative style often combines elements of mythology, history, and contemporary society.
 
 
 
• **Magical Realism**
 
 
• A literary genre in which magical elements are a natural part of an otherwise mundane, realistic environment.
 
• It is characterized by a realistic view of the modern world while also adding magical elements.
 
• Gabriel García Márquez's "One Hundred Years of Solitude" is a seminal example of this genre.
 
• Rushdie's works often incorporate magical realism, blending fantasy with reality.
 
 
 
• **Booker Prize**
 
 
• A prestigious literary award given each year for the best original novel written in the English language and published in the UK.
 
• Established in 1969, it is one of the leading literary awards in the English-speaking world.
 
• Salman Rushdie's "Midnight's Children" won the Booker Prize and was later awarded the Booker of Bookers.
 
• The prize aims to reward the finest in fiction and highlight the importance of literary achievements.
 
 
 
• **Science Fiction and Fantasy**
 
 
• Genres of speculative fiction that explore imaginative and futuristic concepts such as advanced science and technology, space exploration, time travel, parallel universes, and extraterrestrial life.
 
• Science fiction often deals with the impact of imagined innovations in science or technology on society.
 
• Fantasy typically involves magic, mythical creatures, and supernatural events.
 
• Rushdie's "Grimus" is an example of a novel that blends these genres.

questions.question: Minister of state can attend the cabinet meeting ________.

options.text: only when the speaker invites him

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**only when invited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Minister of State is a junior minister in the Government of India or other countries.
 
• They usually do not hold independent charge of a ministry but assist a cabinet minister in their duties.
 
• They can attend cabinet meetings only when specifically invited to do so.
 
• The invitation is typically extended by the Prime Minister or the head of the cabinet.
 
• Attendance is often based on the relevance of the topic being discussed in the cabinet meeting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cabinet Minister**

 
 
• A senior minister in charge of a particular ministry.
 
• They have the authority to make decisions on policy matters within their ministry.
 
• Cabinet ministers are usually members of the cabinet, the main decision-making body in the government.
 
 
 
• **Minister of State (Independent Charge)**
 
 
• A junior minister who is in charge of a ministry but not part of the cabinet.
 
• They report directly to the Prime Minister or the Cabinet Minister.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Meetings**
 
 
• Regular meetings held by the cabinet to discuss and decide on various government policies and issues.
 
• Attended primarily by cabinet ministers, with other ministers invited as needed.
 
 
 
• **Role of Prime Minister**
 
 
• The head of the government and the chief advisor to the President of India.
 
• Responsible for coordinating the work of different ministries and overseeing the implementation of government policies.

questions.question: In which of the following places were the remains of Mahaparinirvana Buddha found? It is at this location that a 6.1 m long reclining Buddha has been constructed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kushinagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kushinagar is an important Buddhist pilgrimage site located in Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• It is believed to be the place where Gautama Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana (final nirvana) after his death.
 
• Archaeological excavations have revealed several stupas and viharas, which date back to the 3rd century BCE to the 5th century CE.
 
• A prominent feature of Kushinagar is the 6.1-meter-long reclining statue of Buddha, depicting him on his deathbed, which is housed in the Mahaparinirvana Temple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahaparinirvana:** Refers to the final death of an enlightened being who has achieved Nirvana, after which they are released from the cycle of birth and death.
 
• **Reclining Buddha:** A statue or image of Buddha lying down, often symbolizing his last moments and entry into Mahaparinirvana.
 
• **Stupas:** Dome-shaped structures erected as Buddhist shrines, often containing relics of Buddha or other saints.
 
• **Viharas:** Buddhist monasteries that served as places of residence for monks and centers of learning.
 
• **Buddhist Pilgrimage Sites:** Significant locations for followers of Buddhism, such as Lumbini (birthplace of Buddha), Bodh Gaya (site of enlightenment), Sarnath (first teaching), and Kushinagar (place of Mahaparinirvana).

questions.question: The term 'checkmate' is used in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chess**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Checkmate' is a term used in the game of Chess to indicate that a player's king is in a position to be captured ('in check') and there is no possible move to escape the threat.
 
• The objective of chess is to checkmate the opponent's king, thereby winning the game.
 
• The term originates from the Persian phrase 'Shah Mat,' which means 'the king is dead' or 'the king is helpless.'
 
• Checkmate ends the game immediately, and the player whose king has been checkmated loses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chess Pieces:**

 
 
• Each player starts with 16 pieces: 1 king, 1 queen, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, and 8 pawns.
 
• Each piece moves differently; for instance, the rook moves in straight lines, while the bishop moves diagonally.
 
 
 
• **Chessboard Layout:**
 
 
• The chessboard consists of 64 squares in an 8x8 grid, alternating in color (usually black and white).
 
• The pieces are set up in two rows at the beginning of the game, with pawns in the front row and the other pieces behind them.
 
 
 
• **Basic Rules:**
 
 
• Players alternate turns, moving one piece per turn.
 
• The goal is to checkmate the opponent's king while protecting your own king from being checkmated.
 
• Other important concepts include 'stalemate' (a draw) and 'castling' (a special move involving the king and a rook).
 
 
 
• **Chess Notation:**
 
 
• Moves are recorded using algebraic notation, which helps players review and analyze games.
 
• For example, 'e4' indicates moving a pawn to the e4 square, and 'Nf3' indicates moving a knight to the f3 square.

questions.question: Which king of the Mauryan dynasty succeeded Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bindusara was the second Mauryan emperor and the son of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya Empire.
 
• He reigned from approximately 297 BCE to 273 BCE, succeeding his father Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• Bindusara is known for expanding the Mauryan Empire further into central India, consolidating the regions acquired by his father.
 
• He maintained the administrative structure established by Chandragupta and further strengthened the empire's governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the Maurya Empire, one of the largest empires in Indian history.
 
• He established the empire in 322 BCE with the help of his advisor Chanakya.
 
• Chandragupta's reign marked the beginning of a centralized and bureaucratic government in India.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka:**
 
 
• He was one of the most famous Mauryan emperors and the son of Bindusara.
 
• Ashoka is renowned for his role in spreading Buddhism across Asia after his conversion following the Kalinga War.
 
• His reign from 268 BCE to 232 BCE is noted for the promotion of dharma (moral law) and non-violence.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Administration:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire had a highly organized and efficient administration.
 
• It was divided into provinces, each governed by a viceroy appointed by the emperor.
 
• There was a strong emphasis on law and order, with a well-maintained spy system to ensure stability.
 
 
 
• **Economic Policies:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire had a prosperous economy based on agriculture, trade, and commerce.
 
• Bindusara promoted trade with foreign countries, including Greece and Persia.
 
• There were state-controlled industries such as mining, weaving, and metallurgy.

questions.question: The famous Chinese Buddhist pilgrim, Fa Hein visited India during the reign of which of the following Gupta rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fa Hein, a famous Chinese Buddhist monk and pilgrim, visited India during the reign of **Chandragupta II**.
 
• Chandragupta II, also known as **Vikramaditya**, ruled from approximately 380 to 415 CE.
 
• Fa Hein traveled to India in 399 CE and stayed until 414 CE, documenting his journey in his travelogue "Fo-Kuo Ki" (A Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms).
 
• His visit was primarily motivated by his interest in Buddhist texts and the quest for original Buddhist scriptures.
 
• During his stay, Fa Hein visited several significant Buddhist sites, including Pataliputra (modern-day Patna), Kapilavastu, and Lumbini.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)**

 
 
• He was one of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta Empire, known for his military prowess and cultural achievements.
 
• His reign is often considered the golden age of ancient India due to the flourishing of arts, science, and literature.
 
• He extended the Gupta Empire through military conquests and strategic marriages.
 
• Chandragupta II is credited with the defeat of the Shakas (Western Kshatrapas) and the annexation of their territory.
 
 
 
• **Fa Hein's Travelogue**
 
 
• Fa Hein's travelogue provides detailed accounts of the social, economic, and religious conditions of India during Chandragupta II's reign.
 
• His writings offer valuable insights into the practice of Buddhism and the monastic life of that period.
 
• Fa Hein's observations highlight the prosperity and stability of the Gupta Empire under Chandragupta II.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire's Contributions**
 
 
• The Gupta period is renowned for significant advancements in astronomy, mathematics, and metallurgy.
 
• Notable scholars like Aryabhata and Kalidasa thrived during this era, making substantial contributions to their respective fields.
 
• The concept of zero and the decimal system were developed and refined during the Gupta period.

questions.question: Who coined the name ‘Pakistan’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaudhry Rehmat Ali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chaudhry Rehmat Ali** is credited with coining the name 'Pakistan'.
 
• He introduced the name in his pamphlet titled "Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish Forever?" published in **1933**.
 
• The term 'Pakistan' is a combination of letters from the names of the Muslim homelands in South Asia: Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh, and Balochistan.
 
• Rehmat Ali was a key figure in the Pakistan Movement, advocating for a separate nation for Muslims in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• His idea significantly influenced the All-India Muslim League's demand for the creation of Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakistan Movement**

 
 
• The Pakistan Movement was a political movement aimed at the creation of Pakistan as a separate nation for Muslims in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The movement was led by the All-India Muslim League under the leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
 
• It culminated in the partition of British India and the creation of Pakistan on August 14, 1947.
 
 
 
• **All-India Muslim League**
 
 
• The All-India Muslim League was a political party established in 1906 in British India.
 
• Its primary aim was to represent the interests of the Muslim community and work towards the creation of an independent Muslim state.
 
• The party played a crucial role in the Pakistan Movement and the eventual creation of Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Resolution**
 
 
• The Lahore Resolution, also known as the Pakistan Resolution, was passed on March 23, 1940, by the All-India Muslim League.
 
• It called for separate states for Muslims in the north-western and eastern zones of India, leading to the demand for Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Chaudhry Rehmat Ali**
 
 
• Born in 1897, Rehmat Ali was a Pakistani nationalist who played a key role in advocating for the creation of Pakistan.
 
• He passed away in 1951 and is remembered for his significant contributions to the Pakistan Movement.

questions.question: As per Köppen climate classification, the climate of which place is classified as 'Cwg' (meso thermal with dry winters)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gangetic plains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Köppen climate classification system categorizes the Gangetic plains' climate as 'Cwg' which stands for mesothermal climate with dry winters.
 
• This classification indicates a region with a significant temperature difference between summer and winter, with a dry winter season.
 
• The Gangetic plains experience hot summers, with temperatures often exceeding 40°C (104°F).
 
• Winters in the Gangetic plains are mild to cool, with average temperatures ranging from 10°C to 20°C (50°F to 68°F).
 
• This region receives the majority of its annual precipitation during the monsoon season, which typically lasts from June to September.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Köppen Climate Classification**

 
 
• Developed by Wladimir Köppen, this system classifies the world's climates based on average temperature and precipitation.
 
• The classification uses a combination of letters to describe the climate characteristics of a region.
 
• It is one of the most widely used climate classification systems in the world.
 
 
 
• **Meso Thermal Climate**
 
 
• Also known as temperate climates, these regions have moderate temperatures.
 
• They typically experience distinct seasonal changes, including warm summers and cool winters.
 
• Meso thermal climates are divided into several types, including humid subtropical, Mediterranean, and oceanic climates.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Season**
 
 
• A seasonal wind pattern that brings significant rainfall to many parts of the world, particularly South Asia.
 
• In India, the monsoon season generally starts in June and lasts until September.
 
• Monsoon rains are crucial for agriculture, which is a major part of the economy in the Gangetic plains.
 
 
 
• **Gangetic Plains**
 
 
• Also known as the Indo-Gangetic plains, this region spans northern India, covering states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
 
• The plains are known for their fertile soil, making them one of the most agriculturally productive regions in the world.
 
• The region is densely populated and plays a significant role in the economy and culture of India.

questions.question: In order to preserve pickles, a mixture of 5% to 8% of acetic acid in water is used. This preservative is also commonly known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vinegar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vinegar is a liquid consisting mainly of acetic acid (CH3COOH) and water.
 
• The acetic acid concentration in vinegar typically ranges between 5% and 8%, making it suitable for pickling and preserving food.
 
• It is commonly used as a preservative because its acidic nature inhibits the growth of harmful bacteria.
 
• Vinegar is also used for culinary purposes, including flavoring and marinating foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Vinegar**

 
 
• **White Vinegar:** Made from grain alcohol and often used for pickling and cleaning.
 
• **Apple Cider Vinegar:** Made from fermented apple juice, known for its health benefits.
 
• **Balsamic Vinegar:** Originates from Italy and has a rich, complex flavor, often used in salads and gourmet dishes.
 
• **Rice Vinegar:** Common in Asian cuisine, known for its mild and slightly sweet taste.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits of Vinegar**
 
 
• Vinegar can help in controlling blood sugar levels.
 
• It has antimicrobial properties, making it useful in food preservation and cleaning.
 
• Vinegar may aid in weight loss by promoting a feeling of fullness.
 
• It is known to have antioxidant properties.
 
 
 
• **Production of Vinegar**
 
 
• Vinegar is produced through the fermentation of ethanol by acetic acid bacteria.
 
• The fermentation process involves two stages: alcoholic fermentation and acetic fermentation.
 
• Commercial vinegar production often uses a fast fermentation process known as the submerged fermentation method.
